sections.content: Billings, Montana does not always make the headlines in real estate investing circles, but that is exactly what makes it interesting. While investors chase overheated markets in Phoenix or Austin, Billings quietly offers affordable home prices, steady population growth, and a diversified local economy that supports both rentals and resale flips. Whether you are a seasoned wholesaler or just getting started, it pays to understand the fundamentals of secondary markets like this one. If you are brand new to the space, check out our guide to Real Estate Investing for Beginners before diving in. For everyone else, let's get into what makes Billings worth your attention right now.
Billings MT Market Overview: What Investors Need to Know

Billings is the largest city in Montana, with a population of roughly 120,000 people and growing. It sits at the intersection of energy, healthcare, agriculture, and transportation industries, which creates a stable economic base that is less vulnerable to single-sector downturns. The city is home to two major medical centers, including Billings Clinic and St. Vincent Healthcare, which collectively employ thousands of residents. That healthcare workforce alone drives consistent demand for mid-range rentals. Meanwhile, the nearby Bakken oil formation and regional agriculture sector attract blue-collar workers who need affordable housing year-round. This economic diversity is a green flag for investors looking for long-term stability over speculative gains.
Average Home Prices and Market Data

As of 2024, the median home price in Billings sits around $320,000 to $340,000, which is significantly lower than the national median in many comparable metros. Entry-level properties in older neighborhoods can still be found in the $150,000 to $220,000 range, making them viable candidates for both wholesale assignments and light rehab flips. Rent prices for a three-bedroom single-family home typically range from $1,400 to $1,900 per month depending on condition and location. That rent-to-price ratio is attractive enough to pencil out buy-and-hold deals, especially when you factor in Montana's relatively low property tax rates. Days on market for distressed properties average around 45 to 60 days, giving investors a reasonable window to make offers without extreme competition.

Before making any offer in Billings, run your numbers through our free ARV Calculator to estimate after-repair value using local comparable sales. A deal that looks good on the surface can fall apart fast if your ARV is off by even 10 percent.
Best Neighborhoods for Real Estate Investors in Billings
Not all parts of Billings carry the same opportunity. Knowing where to focus your efforts can save you months of wasted time chasing deals in the wrong zip codes.
South Side: High Rental Demand, Lower Entry Points

The South Side of Billings is one of the most active areas for investors. Properties here tend to be older, built in the 1950s through 1970s, which means you will find more distressed inventory and motivated sellers. Homes often sell in the $150,000 to $210,000 range, and rental demand is strong from workforce tenants. This area is well-suited for wholesale deals, small flips, and buy-and-hold rentals targeting working-class renters.
Heights: Growing Suburb with Family Appeal

The Heights neighborhood sits on the east side of Billings and has seen steady residential growth over the past decade. It attracts families and young professionals, and home values tend to be slightly higher, ranging from $220,000 to $310,000. Fix-and-flip opportunities exist here when you can source properties below market value. The resale market in the Heights is more active, meaning you can move renovated properties faster than in some other parts of the city.
Downtown and Midtown: Emerging Value-Add Plays

Billings has invested significantly in downtown revitalization in recent years. Small multifamily properties and mixed-use buildings near the downtown core are attracting attention from investors who want long-term appreciation alongside cash flow. While entry prices are higher here, value-add opportunities exist for investors willing to do light commercial repositioning or convert older properties into short-term rentals targeting business travelers and medical tourists visiting the hospital corridor.
Types of Real Estate Deals Available in Billings MT

items: Wholesale Deals: Billings has a healthy supply of motivated sellers, including probate situations, pre-foreclosures, and tired landlords looking to exit. Assignment fees in the $8,000 to $20,000 range are common on deals in the South Side and older Midtown corridors. For a step-by-step breakdown of the wholesaling process, read our guide to Wholesaling Real Estate for Beginners.

Fix and Flip: Billings supports active flipping when you buy right. Aim for properties at 65 to 70 percent of ARV minus repairs. Renovation costs for a standard 3-bed, 1-bath South Side house typically run $25,000 to $50,000 depending on condition. Flip timelines average 4 to 6 months including acquisition, rehab, and resale.

Buy-and-Hold Rentals: Long-term rentals work well in Billings due to the steady workforce population. A property bought at $180,000, rented at $1,500 per month, can generate a gross yield above 10 percent. Factor in vacancy, maintenance, and management before finalizing your numbers.

Small Multifamily: Duplexes and small apartment buildings are available in several Billings neighborhoods. These are excellent for house-hacking strategies or building a portfolio of 2 to 4 unit properties that qualify for conventional financing.

Short-Term Rentals: Billings sees consistent business travel and medical-related extended stays. A well-positioned furnished rental near Billings Clinic or St. Vincent can generate $2,200 to $3,000 per month, outperforming traditional long-term rents in the right location.

sections.content: Local Market Trends Shaping Investment Decisions

Billings has seen modest but consistent home price appreciation over the past five years, averaging 4 to 6 percent annually. That pace is slower than coastal markets but also more sustainable, meaning less risk of a sharp correction. Inventory remains tight across the board, with fewer than 400 active listings on the MLS at any given time, which actually favors investors who can source deals off-market. New construction activity is concentrated in the Heights and far west side, keeping older housing stock in other neighborhoods relevant for value-add investors. Interest rate sensitivity has cooled some retail buyer demand, which opens doors for cash investors willing to move quickly. You can track ongoing deal activity and market shifts for this city through our dedicated Billings MT market page.

The best real estate deals are rarely found on the MLS. In secondary markets like Billings, the real money is made by those who build systems to find motivated sellers before the competition even knows the property exists.
Practical Tips for Out-of-State Investors

Investing remotely in Billings is absolutely doable, but it requires building the right local team before you commit capital. Start by identifying a property management company with experience in the neighborhoods you are targeting. Interview at least three options and ask specifically about tenant placement timelines and average vacancy rates for their portfolio. Next, find a local real estate attorney familiar with Montana's landlord-tenant laws and title requirements. Montana is a deed of trust state, which affects how foreclosures and title transfers work. You will also want a relationship with a local contractor who can provide reliable rehab estimates and turn projects around on schedule.

Finding deals from out of state is where technology makes the biggest difference. Learning how to find off-market real estate deals is critical in a smaller market like Billings where the best opportunities are never publicly listed. Direct mail campaigns targeting probate leads, pre-foreclosures, and absentee owners in South Side zip codes consistently produce motivated seller inquiries. Once you have a lead, you need to be able to analyze it fast. Our free Wholesale Deal Calculator lets you plug in purchase price, repair costs, and ARV to instantly see your potential profit margin before you pick up the phone.

When visiting Billings for due diligence, schedule your trip to drive neighborhoods during both morning and evening hours. What looks like a clean street at noon can tell a very different story at 7pm. Local context matters enormously for pricing rental demand accurately.

Finally, do not skip the underwriting step just because Billings feels affordable. A $180,000 purchase price can still be a bad deal if your repair estimates are wrong or the rental market in that specific pocket is softer than average. Always run conservative numbers, use local comps from the past 90 days, and build in a buffer of at least 10 to 15 percent on your rehab budget. Learning how to analyze real estate deals like a pro is a skill that pays dividends in every market, especially when you are operating from a distance.
